angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 799,359 km at 161.14 pc = 0.07 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 6.2059 +/- 0.0193 mas (same row, RUWE 0.86): 161.14 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.149 +/- 0.067 solar radii from Christiansen et al. 2022, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-376 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163..244C/abstract): 799,359 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.908 +/- 0.394 solar masses from Christiansen et al. 2022, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-376 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163..244C/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5937 +/- 138 K from Christiansen et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-376 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163..244C/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Christiansen et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-376 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163..244C/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-376.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.276, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
